symptoms: Tiny yellow-white speckles (stipples) on the upper leaf surface
Fine webbing on leaf undersides and between leaves in heavy attack
Leaves bronze, dry and drop; mites are dust-sized moving dots under leaves
Damage starts at field edges and spreads in hot dry weather

severity_cues.advanced: Webbing, bronzing across plants, leaf drop

favorable_conditions: Hot (above 28 C), dry, dusty conditions; over-fertilized dense foliage; drought-stressed plants

treatment.summary: Hit the underside of leaves with a repeat spray, and reduce heat and dust stress
steps: Spray Wettable sulphur 80 WP at 2.0 g per litre, covering the leaf undersides
Repeat once after 7 days to catch newly hatched mites
Avoid spraying sulphur when temperature crosses 32 C, it can burn leaves
Avoid over-use of broad-spectrum insecticides, they kill natural mite enemies and flare the pest

products.name: Wettable sulphur 80 WP
products.label_source: CIB&RC registered label, waiting period 3 days

organic: Neem oil 1500 ppm at 3 ml per litre, repeat every 5 days, underside coverage
Strong water spray to knock mites off in the morning
Conserve predatory mites and ladybird beetles by not spraying broad-spectrum poisons

source.org: TNAU Agritech Portal, crop protection, tomato pests
source.title: Tomato: mite management

safety_notes: Wear gloves, mask and full sleeves while spraying
Do not harvest within 3 days of sulphur spray, and never spray sulphur above 32 C
